title: How to use a needle threader
subtitle: The wire loop method for threading fine needles quickly.
excerpt: A needle threader makes light work of threading any needle whose eye is too small to see clearly. The wire loop goes through the eye first, the thread goes through the loop, then everything pulls back through together.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Needle preparation and threading aids.
Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746. Needlework equipment notes.

glossaryTerms.definition: The thin diamond-shaped wire attached to the flat handle of a needle threader. It passes through the needle eye to carry the thread through.

content.text: A needle threader takes the fine motor effort out of threading a needle. You push the rigid
through the eye instead of the thread, then let the loop carry the thread through. The whole thing takes three seconds when your hands know the sequence.
How to thread with the threader
Hold the needle in your non-dominant hand with the eye facing up. Steady it against your thumbnail if needed.
Hold the threader by its flat metal or plastic handle in your dominant hand. Push the wire loop through the needle eye from the front.
Pass the cut end of the thread through the wire loop. Leave about 5 cm of thread inside the loop.
Draw the threader handle back through the eye, pulling the loop and the thread with it.
Pull the thread end until about 8 to 10 cm remains as a tail through the eye. Remove the threader wire from the thread.

attrs.heading: What goes wrong
attrs.intro: Three ways the threader fails and how to avoid them.

items.symptom: The wire loop bends and won't go through the eye
items.cause: The wire has been pushed sideways or the needle is held at an angle.
items.fix: Keep the needle upright and approach the eye straight on. If the wire is bent, straighten it gently with fingernails before the next attempt.

items.symptom: The thread bunches up and won't pull through
items.cause: Too many strands were passed through the loop, or the thread was folded back on itself.
items.fix: Pass only the single cut end through the loop, not a fold. For multiple strands, align all the cut ends together before threading them through the loop.

items.cause: Wire threaders have a limited life and break after heavy use, or after being bent sharply.
items.fix: Keep a spare. Most packs contain two or three. Avoid bending the wire at an angle when passing it through the eye.

content.text: A threader helps most with size 26 needles and finer, where the eye is hard to see. The action is worth practising until it feels automatic, as fine-count linen needs re-threading often.
